objective: Ask whether adding one cross-asset trend sleeve (D1 = Carlson's Defense First TAA rotation over TLT/GLD/DBC/UUP with SPY fallback, original published rank weights 40/30/20/10; D2 = the same four assets each held only when its trailing-12-month total return beats SHY's, weighted by inverse 63-session volatility, otherwise SHY) to the live S3 leveraged-momentum sleeve, combined by trailing-63-session inverse-volatility monthly weighting (the same combination math `screen_lane.combine_two_sleeves` ports from `run_h20260927_01_sleeve_combination.combine_portfolio`), raises the combined Sharpe over a volatility-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control by >=0.05 in both the anchor window (2024-01-08..2026-09-17) and the stress period (2016-05-02..2023-09-15) -- the K2 owner-widened bar -- or, failing that, whether D1/D2 standalone clear K1 (offset-median Sharpe >= 80% of S3's own median in both windows, positive CAGR at 20bp). All rebalance-day offsets (21 monthly versions) are swept and judged by the median, per the owner's 2026-09-28 'no cherry-picked rebalance date' rule; no parameter is tuned -- D1 uses Carlson's published rank weights/hurdle/fallback unchanged, D2's 12-month/63-session thresholds are the two round numbers stated in the queue task, not searched.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same frozen contract as every screen_lane batch: select 2023-09-18..2025-12-31, anchor 2024-01-08..2026-09-17 (frozen gate), stress 2016-05-02..2023-09-15 (data starts 2016-01-04, so panel warmup begins 2015-01-02 per screen_lane.PANEL_START; D1's calendar 12-month blend and D2's trailing-12-month/63-session vol first have enough history around 2017-01, matching Defense First's own '2017-01-31 first live' finding in H-20260923-12). 2026-01-02..2026-09-17 holdout is reported but flagged contaminated (already seen for S3 and for D1's SPY-fallback sibling in H-20260923-12). Validity is limited to this specific four-ETF defensive-asset basket (bonds/gold/commodities/dollar) and to the specific combination-with-S3 question; no claim is made that either D1 or D2 generalizes to other trend universes, other combination weights, or other host sleeves.
existing_solution_comparison: Registry dedup (`oc research directions check "cross asset trend sleeve S3 combination TSMOM ETF"`, 2026-09-28) found no exact prior test of this combination question; best match was an unrelated leveraged-SMA-gate direction (score 0.50). Three related local directions exist and are each distinguished here: (1) `dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum` (harvested 2026-09-23) already logs Carlson's 2025 SSRN preprint and its AllocateSmartly/Quantitativo replications -- this round reuses those verified source cards/snapshots unchanged (copied into this dossier's sources/) rather than re-fetching, and adds no new claim about the mechanism itself. (2) `dir:s3_defense_first_remainder` (refuted 2026-09-23, H-20260923-12): that test asked whether S3's *idle SHY remainder* (the ~39% average uninvested slot inside the S3 book itself) should hold a Defense First rotation instead of cash; neither DF01 (SPY fallback) nor DF02 (SHY fallback) cleared +0.10 Sharpe over plain SHY. This round is a different question: D1 is an *independent full-size sleeve held alongside S3* (not a sub-allocation of S3's cash leg), judged by whether the S3+D1 combination beats a vol-matched delevered-S3 control -- the K2 bar this repo now uses for all sleeve-addition questions (H-20260927-01's methodology), not the 'beat SHY' bar H-20260923-12 used. A rule identical to a refuted sub-allocation candidate can still pass a different, harder-to-game combination test; the two are not the same claim and this round says so explicitly rather than silently re-running a refuted rule under a new label. (3) Step 10 Wave 1 F2 cross-asset TSMOM (`reports/research/control/step10-w1-cross-asset-trend-2026-09.md`, not yet in the registry -- pre-dates the 2026-09-23 registry and is backfilled separately by T-20260928-05): tested 12 candidates of cross-sectional-momentum-ranked SPY/QQQ/IWM/EFA/EEM/TLT/IEF/GLD/DBC/VNQ (broad global multi-asset, not the Defense-First-specific TLT/GLD/DBC/UUP basket) purely standalone against a vol-matched SPY benchmark; 0/12 passed (best excess Sharpe 0.65, best excess CAGR +1.33pp). This round differs in universe (4 defensive-only assets, not 10 broad-asset), in mechanism (D1 uses calendar 1/3/6/12-month blended rank vs. Step 10's single-lookback top-n; D2 uses simple 12-month-vs-SHY absolute momentum with inverse-vol sizing, a different published rule), and critically in the judged question: Step 10 asked only whether the sleeve is good standalone (K1-style), this round's primary bar is the combination edge over vol-matched S3 (K2), which Step 10 never tested because S3 (the leveraged-momentum sleeve) postdates it. Momentum mechanism itself is not novel research -- it is the well-published time-series-momentum/trend-following literature (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012 JFE; Hurst-Ooi-Pedersen 2017 JPM, both freshly fetched this pass, snapshots in sources/) -- what this round tests is only the *local combination arithmetic* with our specific S3 sleeve, which no source publishes for us.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether D1 or D2's daily returns are decorrelated enough from S3 in the stress period specifically (not just on average) that the inverse-vol combination clears +0.05 Sharpe over a same-volatility delevered-S3 control in BOTH the anchor and stress windows -- this is exactly what H-20260927-01 found S1/S2 could not do against S3 (too correlated, 0.79-0.83), and is untested for either D1 or D2 locally. The round reports D1/D2's own correlation with S3 in stress, anchor and 2022 alongside the combination edge so a 'no' verdict is diagnosable (too correlated vs. genuinely no combination benefit even though decorrelated).
negative_experiments_checked: dir:paper_sleeve_combination / H-20260927-01 (refuted 0/3): S1/S2/S3 fixed-proportion or inverse-vol combinations never cleared +0.10 Sharpe over vol-matched S3 in both windows because S1-S3 move together (corr 0.79-0.83); this round applies the identical vol-matched-control combination methodology (now widened to the K2 >=0.05 bar) to a mechanistically different, defensive-asset sleeve pair, which is the correct way to re-test the combination question with less-correlated legs rather than assuming the earlier refutation generalizes. dir:s3_defense_first_remainder / H-20260923-12 (refuted): Defense First as a sub-allocation of S3's own idle cash never beat +0.10 Sharpe over plain SHY; distinguished above (different host structure and different pass bar) rather than treated as already answering this round's question. Step 10 W1 F2 cross-asset TSMOM (0/12 standalone, not yet registered): distinguished above by universe and by judged question (standalone-only vs. combination-with-S3).
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Identical to every screen_lane batch: 10bp/side primary, 20bp/side stress, close signal -> next-session-open fill, `salvage.simulate` unchanged. The combination itself charges `combo_cost_bps * sum(abs(delta weight))` on the session after each month-end signal via `screen_lane.combine_two_sleeves` (ported from `combo.combine_portfolio`), at the same 10/20bp. The vol-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control rebalances daily at a per-window fixed k with zero cost (conservative, favors the control).
stop_condition: If neither D1 nor D2 clears K2 (combination Sharpe edge >=0.05 over vol-matched S3 in both anchor and stress) or K1 (standalone offset-median Sharpe >=80% of S3's own median Sharpe in both windows, positive 20bp CAGR), the verdict is: this defensive four-asset trend basket adds no combination value over delevering S3 alone at the same risk, and the live-pilot decision should not add a cross-asset sleeve on this evidence. Reopen only with a new defensive-asset set, a new published combination or sizing rule, or new disclosed data -- not by re-tuning D1/D2's published/round-number parameters or by cherry-picking a rebalance offset.

AQR A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing Hurst Ooi Pedersen

sources.claim: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012, Journal of Financial Economics) document time-series momentum: an asset's own trailing 12-month excess return positively predicts its own future return, and this holds for every one of 58 diverse futures/forward contracts (equity indices, currencies, commodities, sovereign bonds) they examine over 25+ years.
sources.market_and_period: 58 liquid futures and forward contracts (equity indices, currencies, commodities, sovereign bonds), more than 25 years of data through the early 2010s.
sources.applicability: Grounds D2's own-asset absolute-momentum mechanism (hold when trailing 12-month return beats a cash proxy) as a peer-reviewed, independently documented anomaly rather than a home-grown rule; D2's specific thresholds are round numbers from the queue task, not this paper's own parameters.
sources.limitations: Evidence is on liquid futures/forward contracts, not the TLT/GLD/DBC/UUP ETF basket, and not long-only cash-hurdle-screened weights; motivates the mechanism only, not evidence D2 clears this repo's 10/20bp cost contract or combines well with S3.
sources.independent_replication: Peer-reviewed, published in Journal of Financial Economics (2012); re-tested over a much longer sample by the AQR century study below.

sources.claim: Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen (2017, Journal of Portfolio Management) extend time-series-momentum/trend-following evidence back to 1880 using a novel data set, finding the strategy was consistently profitable across the following ~110 years and performed well in 8 of the 10 largest historical crisis periods, with low correlation to traditional stock/bond benchmarks.
sources.market_and_period: Global multi-asset trend-following portfolio (equity index, fixed income, commodity futures, currency forwards), 1880-2016.
sources.applicability: Motivates evaluating D1/D2 across the full stress period (2016-05..2023-09, including 2018Q4, 2020 and 2022 drawdowns) and reporting 2022-specific correlation with S3, rather than relying on the anchor window alone.
sources.limitations: Broad multi-asset futures trend evidence over a century, not this repo's specific defensive ETF basket, cost contract, or combination-with-S3 question; the paper itself flags rising correlations across markets since the credit crisis as a headwind.
sources.independent_replication: Published in Journal of Portfolio Management (2017); extends and corroborates Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen (2012) over a roughly 9x longer sample using an independently constructed historical data set.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Compute D1 and D2's daily-return correlation with the live S3 book in the stress period first (cheap, no simulation needed beyond what the batch run already produces); if either is highly correlated with S3 in stress (>0.6, the rough level H-20260927-01 found disqualifying for S1/S2), the K2 combination edge is unlikely to clear +0.05 in that window and the full batch leaderboard will show it directly.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: D1 or D2 clears K2 (judged combination Sharpe edge >=0.05 in both anchor and stress vs. vol-matched S3) or K1 (standalone offset-median Sharpe >=80% of S3's own median in both windows, positive 20bp CAGR), per `reports/research/screens/h20260928_02_cross_asset/leaderboard.json`.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Neither D1 nor D2 clears K2 or K1 in either window.
